name: Descending Branch of Lateral Circumflex Femoral Artery
origin: Lateral circumflex femoral artery (from profunda femoris, occasionally directly from common femoral artery)
course: Descends obliquely inferolaterally in the intermuscular septum between rectus femoris and vastus lateralis alongside the nerve to vastus lateralis.
branches: Septocutaneous and musculocutaneous perforators (A, B, C)
Muscular branches to vastus lateralis and rectus femoris
Anastomotic branch to lateral superior genicular artery
relations: Runs with paired venae comitantes and motor nerve to vastus lateralis in the groove deep to rectus femoris.
variants: Oblique branch present in ~35% of cases
Origin directly from profunda femoris or transverse branch
clinical_relevance: Primary pedicle of the ALT flap and vastus lateralis muscle flap; allows chimeric skin/muscle/fascia harvest.

references.book: Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Deep Inferior Epigastric Artery (DIEA)
origin: External iliac artery just superior to the inguinal ligament
course: Ascends superomedially in extraperitoneal fat, pierces transversalis fascia, enters posterior surface of rectus abdominis near arcuate line, and divides into medial and lateral rows (Moon–Taylor Types I–III).
relations: Accompanied by paired venae comitantes; runs deep to rectus abdominis and anastomoses with superior epigastric system via choke vessels.
angiosome: Deep inferior epigastric angiosome (anterior abdominal wall)
clinical_relevance: Workhorse vascular pedicle for autologous breast reconstruction (DIEP, MS-TRAM, free TRAM) and pelvic/perineal VRAM.

references.book: Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Superficial Inferior Epigastric Artery (SIEA)
origin: Common femoral artery 2–3 cm inferior to inguinal ligament (sometimes common trunk with SCIA)
course: Ascends superiorly and slightly medially over the inguinal ligament within the superficial subcutaneous layer deep to Scarpa fascia initially, then superficial.
relations: Accompanied by superficial inferior epigastric vein (SIEV), which often lies more medially and drains into saphenofemoral junction.
variants: Absent or <1.5 mm diameter in 30–65% of patients
clinical_relevance: Allows breast reconstruction without incising anterior rectus fascia; perfusion rarely crosses the midline reliably.

references.book: Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Thoracodorsal Artery
origin: Terminal continuation of subscapular artery after takeoff of circumflex scapular artery
course: Descends along the deep lateral border of latissimus dorsi in the posterior axilla, entering the hilum ~8–10 cm inferior to the axillary artery.
relations: Travels with thoracodorsal vein and thoracodorsal nerve (C6–C8) forming the neurovascular hilum.
variants: Direct origin from axillary artery in rare cases; variable number of serratus branches
clinical_relevance: Supports latissimus dorsi, TDAP, serratus anterior, and scapular-tip chimeric reconstructions.

name: Radial Artery
origin: Bifurcation of brachial artery in cubital fossa
course: Courses distally along the volar-radial forearm deep to brachioradialis proximally and superficial between brachioradialis and flexor carpi radialis distally.
branches: Septocutaneous perforators in lateral intermuscular septum
relations: Paired venae comitantes plus superficial cephalic vein; superficial branch of radial nerve lies lateral in proximal two-thirds.
angiosome: Radial artery angiosome (volar and radial forearm)
variants: Incomplete superficial palmar arch (requires Allen test)
clinical_relevance: Primary pedicle of the radial forearm free flap (RFFF) and reverse-flow pedicled radial forearm flap.

references.book: Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Peroneal (Fibular) Artery
origin: Tibioperoneal trunk ~2–3 cm distal to anterior tibial artery takeoff
course: Descends along the posteromedial aspect of the fibula between tibialis posterior and flexor hallucis longus.
branches: Septocutaneous perforators in posterior crural septum
relations: Paired venae comitantes; adjacent to flexor hallucis longus and posterior crural intermuscular septum.
angiosome: Peroneal artery angiosome (lateral leg and lateral heel)
variants: Peronea arteria magna (~1–5% — absolute contraindication to free fibula harvest; confirm with CTA/MRA)
clinical_relevance: Supplies free fibula osteocutaneous flap and peroneal artery perforator propeller flaps.

name: Medial Circumflex Femoral Artery (Ascending Branch to Gracilis)
origin: Profunda femoris artery (occasionally common femoral artery)
course: Passes medially between adductor longus and adductor brevis to enter the deep surface of gracilis 8–10 cm below the pubic tubercle.
branches: Perforators to overlying TUG skin paddle
relations: Accompanied by paired venae comitantes; anterior branch of obturator nerve enters slightly superiorly.
angiosome: Medial circumflex femoral angiosome (proximal medial thigh)
variants: Dual proximal pedicles in a minority of patients
clinical_relevance: Dominant pedicle of gracilis muscle, TUG breast flap, and functional free gracilis for facial reanimation.

references.book: Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Profunda Femoris Artery Perforators (1st–3rd)
course: Pierce adductor magnus posteriorly to emerge in the posterior thigh 3–6 cm inferior to the gluteal fold and posterior to gracilis.
branches: Musculocutaneous and septocutaneous posterior thigh perforators
relations: Course through adductor magnus near posterior femoral cutaneous nerve.
variants: Variable dominance between 1st, 2nd, and 3rd perforators; CTA mapping strongly recommended
clinical_relevance: Basis of the Profunda Artery Perforator (PAP) flap for autologous breast reconstruction.

references.book: Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Superior Gluteal Artery (SGA)
origin: Posterior division of internal iliac artery
course: Exits greater sciatic foramen superior to piriformis and divides into superficial and deep branches piercing gluteus maximus.
relations: Emerges near junction of medial and middle thirds of line between PSIS and greater trochanter.
variants: Short pedicle length if dissection stops at sacral fascia
clinical_relevance: Pedicle of SGAP flap for autologous breast reconstruction and gluteal perforator flaps for sacral pressure injuries.

references.book: Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Thoracoacromial Artery (Pectoral Branch)
course: Pierces clavipectoral fascia and descends on the deep surface of pectoralis major along a line from the acromion to the xiphoid.
branches: Pectoral, deltoid, acromial, and clavicular branches
relations: Accompanied by lateral pectoral nerve on deep surface of pectoralis major.
variants: Secondary segmental blood supply from internal mammary perforators (Mathes–Nahai Type V)
clinical_relevance: Dominant pedicle of the pectoralis major flap for sternal wound and head & neck salvage reconstruction.

references.book: Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Medial Sural Artery
origin: Popliteal artery at level of knee joint
course: Enters proximal medial head of gastrocnemius ~2–4 cm below popliteal crease and gives off musculocutaneous perforators distally.
relations: Paired venae comitantes; tibial nerve branch accompanies pedicle.
variants: 1–4 perforators typically 8–12 cm distal to popliteal crease
clinical_relevance: Supplies medial gastrocnemius muscle flap (knee/proximal tibia) and thin MSAP free flap.

name: Superficial Circumflex Iliac Artery (SCIA)
origin: Femoral artery ~2–3 cm inferior to inguinal ligament
course: Courses superolaterally parallel to and ~2 cm inferior to the inguinal ligament toward the ASIS; divides into superficial and deep branches.
branches: Deep branch (pierces deep fascia lateral to sartorius)
relations: Superficial circumflex iliac vein drains to saphenous bulb; lateral femoral cutaneous nerve crosses nearby.
angiosome: Superficial circumflex iliac angiosome (groin / iliac crest)
variants: Common trunk with SIEA in up to 48% of cases
clinical_relevance: Pedicle of the classic pedicled groin flap for hand coverage and the thin SCIP free flap.

references.book: Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Supratrochlear Artery
course: Exits medial superior orbital rim 1.7–2.2 cm from midline, pierces corrugator supercilii, and ascends vertically in subcutaneous plane over frontalis.
branches: Rich anastomotic plexus with supraorbital and angular arteries
relations: Accompanied by supratrochlear nerve and supratrochlear veins draining to angular vein.
variants: Emergence varies 1.5–2.5 cm from midline; confirm with handheld Doppler
clinical_relevance: Axial pedicle of the paramedian forehead flap — gold standard for major nasal subunit reconstruction.

name: Thoracodorsal Nerve
course: Descends along posterior axillary wall with thoracodorsal vessels to innervate latissimus dorsi.
branches: Lateral and medial motor branches following vascular bifurcation
relations: Must be carefully separated during TDAP harvest to preserve latissimus dorsi motor function.
variants: Early branching proximal to muscle hilum
clinical_relevance: Enables functional muscle transfer (elbow flexion, chest wall) or can be divided in breast reconstruction to prevent animation deformity.

references.book: Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Lateral Femoral Cutaneous Nerve (LFCN)
course: Passes under or through inguinal ligament medial to ASIS and courses subcutaneously across anterolateral thigh.
relations: Superficial to fascia lata; harvested with ALT flap to create a sensate flap.
variants: Variable distance medial to ASIS (0–3 cm)
clinical_relevance: Allows innervated (sensate) ALT reconstruction for oral cavity, phalloplasty, or plantar foot defects.

references.book: Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications
